declarations.documentation:
Construct PMF rows from a nonnegative Real matrix whose finite rows sum to one.
No clipping or rescaling changes its coordinates under these premises.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.channelOfRealMatrix
declarations.type:
{alpha : Type u} →
  {beta : Type v} →
    [inst : Fintype.{v} beta] →
      (A : Matrix.{u, v, 0} alpha beta ℝ) →
        (∀ (x : alpha) (y : beta), LE.le.{0} 0 (A x y)) →
          (∀ (x : alpha), Eq.{1} (∑ y, A x y) 1) → alpha → PMF.{v} beta

declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.channelOfRealMatrix_apply
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Fintype.{v} beta] (A : Matrix.{u, v, 0} alpha beta ℝ)
  (hn : ∀ (x : alpha) (y : beta), LE.le.{0} 0 (A x y)) (hs : ∀ (x : alpha), Eq.{1} (∑ y, A x y) 1) (x : alpha)
  (y : beta),
  Eq.{1} ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.channelOfRealMatrix.{u, v} A hn hs x) y) (ENNReal.ofReal (A x y))

declarations.documentation: Taking Real coordinates and reconstructing returns the original semantic channel.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.channelOfRealMatrix_realMatrix
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Fintype.{v} beta] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),

    (Decidable.decide
      (Membership.mem.{u, u} (↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnPattern.{u, v} kappa y)) x))

∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)

  (y : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa)) (x : alpha),
  Eq.{1}
    (HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.realMatrix.{u, v} kappa x ↑y)
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnValue.{u, v} kappa hSingular y).toReal)
    (bif
        Decidable.decide
          (Membership.mem.{u, u} (↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnPattern.{u, v} kappa y)) x) then

declarations.documentation:
Positive values and nonempty patterns representing the same exact column
are unique. No strict upper bound or pre-assumed finiteness is required.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnData_unique
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)
  (hSingular : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa)
  (y : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa)) (t : Finset.{u} alpha),
  Finset.Nonempty.{u} t →
    ∀ (w : ENNReal),
      LT.lt.{0} 0 w →
        (∀ (x : alpha), Eq.{1} ((kappa x) ↑y) (ite.{1} (Membership.mem.{u, u} t x) w 0)) →
          Eq.{u + 1} t ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnPattern.{u, v} kappa y) ∧
            Eq.{1} w (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnValue.{u, v} kappa hSingular y)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem columnData_unique [Fintype alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF beta)

declarations.documentation:
Real uniqueness follows by exact ofReal recovery of the PMF entries. The
candidate Real value needs positivity, not a separate upper-bound premise.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnData_toReal_unique
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)
  (hSingular : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa)
  (y : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa)) (t : Finset.{u} alpha),
  Finset.Nonempty.{u} t →
    ∀ (w : ℝ),
      LT.lt.{0} 0 w →
        (∀ (x : alpha), Eq.{1} ((kappa x) ↑y).toReal (ite.{1} (Membership.mem.{u, u} t x) w 0)) →
          Eq.{u + 1} t ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnPattern.{u, v} kappa y) ∧
            Eq.{1} w (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnValue.{u, v} kappa hSingular y).toReal
declarations.source_line_text: theorem columnData_toReal_unique [Fintype alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF beta)

declarations.documentation:
Equal entries after an input equivalence preserve the admitted value.
Outputs may live in unrelated universes and need not be finite.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnValue_transport
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} {alpha' : Type u'} {beta' : Type v'} (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)
  (eta : alpha' → PMF.{v'} beta') (hKappa : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa)
  (hEta : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u', v'} eta)
  (y : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa))
  (z : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u', v'} eta))
  (eX : Equiv.{u + 1, u' + 1} alpha alpha'),
  (∀ (x : alpha), Eq.{1} ((eta (eX x)) ↑z) ((kappa x) ↑y)) →
    Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnValue.{u', v'} eta hEta z)
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnValue.{u, v} kappa hKappa y)

declarations.documentation:
Actual column transport maps the input support by the forward equivalence;
membership on the new alphabet consequently uses its inverse.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnPattern_transport
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} {alpha' : Type u'} {beta' : Type v'} [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{u'} alpha'] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (eta : alpha' → PMF.{v'} beta')
  (y : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa))
  (z : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u', v'} eta))
  (eX : Equiv.{u + 1, u' + 1} alpha alpha'),
  (∀ (x : alpha), Eq.{1} ((eta (eX x)) ↑z) ((kappa x) ↑y)) →
    Eq.{u' + 1} (↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnPattern.{u', v'} eta z))
      (Finset.map.{u, u'} (Equiv.toEmbedding.{u + 1, u' + 1} eX)
        ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.columnPattern.{u, v} kappa y))
declarations.source_line_text: theorem columnPattern_transport {alpha' : Type u'} {beta' : Type v'}

declarations.documentation:

with the inverse vector transport covering every finite vector.

declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} α] [inst_1 : Nonempty.{u + 1} α]
  (D : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.CompressedPatternData.{u} α)
  (y : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.OccurringPattern.{u} D → ℝ) {m n : ℕ}

  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Dual.Feasible.{u} D y ↔
    (∀ (i : Fin m), LE.le.{0} 0 (Function.comp.{1, u + 1, 1} y (⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} rows)) i)) ∧
      ∀ (j : Fin n),
        LE.le.{0} 1
          (Matrix.mulVec.{0, 0, 0}
            (Matrix.transpose.{0, 0, 0}
              ((Matrix.reindex.{0, 0, u, u, 0} rows cols)
                (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.reducedMatrix.{u} D)))
            (Function.comp.{1, u + 1, 1} y ⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} rows)) j)

declarations.documentation:
The entire finite-coordinate attained objective image equals the intrinsic
image. The inverse vector `z ∘ rows` covers every finite vector, including when
the partition presentation has no coordinates.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Dual.objectiveValues_reindex
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} α] [inst_1 : Nonempty.{u + 1} α]
  (D : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.CompressedPatternData.{u} α) {m n : ℕ}
  (rows : Equiv.{u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.OccurringPattern.{u} D) (Fin m))
  (cols : Equiv.{u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.AdmissiblePartition.{u} D) (Fin n)),
  Eq.{1}
    (Set.image.{0, 0}
      (fun z =>
        dotProduct.{0, 0}
          (Function.comp.{1, u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.CompressedPatternData.value.{u} D)
            ⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} rows))
          z)
      (Set.ofPred.{0} fun z =>
        (∀ (i : Fin m), LE.le.{0} 0 (z i)) ∧
          ∀ (j : Fin n),
            LE.le.{0} 1
              (Matrix.mulVec.{0, 0, 0}
                (Matrix.transpose.{0, 0, 0}
                  ((Matrix.reindex.{0, 0, u, u, 0} rows cols)
                    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.reducedMatrix.{u} D)))
                z j)))
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Dual.objectiveValues.{u} D)

declarations.documentation:
Supplied row and column enumerations preserve both the vector equation and
coefficient nonnegativity. This applies to either incidence system and to input
incidence, including zero columns; it makes no feasibility assertion.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.system_reindex_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {I : Type v} {J : Type w} [inst : Fintype.{w} J] {m n : ℕ} (M : Matrix.{v, w, 0} I J ℝ) (value : I → ℝ)
  (weight : J → ℝ) (rows : Equiv.{v + 1, 1} I (Fin m)) (cols : Equiv.{w + 1, 1} J (Fin n)),
  (∀ (j : Fin n), LE.le.{0} 0 (Function.comp.{1, w + 1, 1} weight (⇑(Equiv.symm.{w + 1, 1} cols)) j)) ∧
      Eq.{1}
        (Matrix.mulVec.{0, 0, 0} ((Matrix.reindex.{0, 0, v, w, 0} rows cols) M)
          (Function.comp.{1, w + 1, 1} weight ⇑(Equiv.symm.{w + 1, 1} cols)))
        (Function.comp.{1, v + 1, 1} value ⇑(Equiv.symm.{v + 1, 1} rows)) ↔
    (∀ (j : J), LE.le.{0} 0 (weight j)) ∧ Eq.{v + 1} (Matrix.mulVec.{0, v, w} M weight) value
declarations.source_line_text: theorem system_reindex_iff (M : Matrix I J ℝ) (value : I → ℝ) (weight : J → ℝ)

  (κ : α → PMF.{v} β) (hκ : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} κ),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} κ ↔
    IsGreatest.{0}
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Primal.objectiveValues.{u}
        (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.compressedPatternData.{u, v} κ hκ))
      1

declarations.documentation:
Independent finite row and column presentations preserve primal feasibility,
with pointwise inequalities and inverse coordinate transport.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Primal.feasible_reindex_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} α] [inst_1 : Nonempty.{u + 1} α]
  (D : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.CompressedPatternData.{u} α)
  (x : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.AdmissiblePartition.{u} D → ℝ) {m n : ℕ}
  (rows : Equiv.{u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.OccurringPattern.{u} D) (Fin m))
  (cols : Equiv.{u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.AdmissiblePartition.{u} D) (Fin n)),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Primal.Feasible.{u} D x ↔
    (∀ (j : Fin n), LE.le.{0} 0 (Function.comp.{1, u + 1, 1} x (⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} cols)) j)) ∧
      ∀ (i : Fin m),
        LE.le.{0}
          (Matrix.mulVec.{0, 0, 0}
            ((Matrix.reindex.{0, 0, u, u, 0} rows cols)
              (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.reducedMatrix.{u} D))
            (Function.comp.{1, u + 1, 1} x ⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} cols)) i)
          (Function.comp.{1, u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.CompressedPatternData.value.{u} D)
            (⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} rows)) i)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem feasible_reindex_iff (x : AdmissiblePartition D → ℝ) {m n : ℕ}

declarations.documentation:
The entire finite-coordinate objective image equals the intrinsic image.
The inverse vector map covers every finite vector, including empty columns.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Primal.objectiveValues_reindex
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} α] [inst_1 : Nonempty.{u + 1} α]
  (D : PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.CompressedPatternData.{u} α) {m n : ℕ}
  (rows : Equiv.{u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.OccurringPattern.{u} D) (Fin m))
  (cols : Equiv.{u + 1, 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.AdmissiblePartition.{u} D) (Fin n)),
  Eq.{1}
    (Set.image.{0, 0} (fun z => ∑ j, z j)
      (Set.ofPred.{0} fun z =>
        (∀ (j : Fin n), LE.le.{0} 0 (z j)) ∧
          ∀ (i : Fin m),
            LE.le.{0}
              (Matrix.mulVec.{0, 0, 0}
                ((Matrix.reindex.{0, 0, u, u, 0} rows cols)
                  (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Incidence.reducedMatrix.{u} D))
                z i)
              (Function.comp.{1, u + 1, 1}
                (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.CompressedPatternData.value.{u} D)
                (⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} rows)) i)))
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.Primal.objectiveValues.{u} D)

declarations.documentation:
A joint law with the prescribed first and second marginals.
This predicate itself requires no finiteness assumption.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling
declarations.type: {beta : Type u} → PMF.{u} beta → PMF.{u} beta → PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta) → Prop
declarations.source_line_text: def IsCoupling {beta : Type u} (p q : PMF beta) (g : PMF (beta × beta)) : Prop :=

declarations.documentation: Every diagonal atom is bounded by each prescribed marginal atom.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.apply_diag_le_min
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [Finite.{u + 1} beta] {p q : PMF.{u} beta} {g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.{u} p q g →
    ∀ (y : beta), LE.le.{0} (g (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y)) (Min.min.{0} (p y) (q y))

declarations.documentation: Finite total variation with the paper's half-L1 normalization.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV
declarations.type: {beta : Type u} → [Fintype.{u} beta] → PMF.{u} beta → PMF.{u} beta → ℝ
declarations.source_line_text: noncomputable def finiteTV (p q : PMF beta) : ℝ :=

declarations.documentation: The exact total mass shared by two finite laws.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass
declarations.type: {beta : Type u} → [Fintype.{u} beta] → PMF.{u} beta → PMF.{u} beta → ENNReal
declarations.source_line_text: noncomputable def overlapMass (p q : PMF beta) : ℝ≥0∞ :=

declarations.documentation: Shared mass does not depend on the order of the laws.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass_comm
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q)
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} q p)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem overlapMass_comm (p q : PMF beta) : overlapMass p q = overlapMass q p := by

declarations.documentation: Shared mass is at most the total mass of either law.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass_le_one
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  LE.le.{0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q) 1
declarations.source_line_text: theorem overlapMass_le_one (p q : PMF beta) : overlapMass p q ≤ 1 := by

declarations.documentation: In particular, shared mass is finite, as required for real conversion.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass_ne_top
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Ne.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q) Top.top.{0}
declarations.source_line_text: theorem overlapMass_ne_top (p q : PMF beta) : overlapMass p q ≠ ∞ :=

declarations.documentation: Exact overlap converts to the sum of the real pointwise minima.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass_toReal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q).toReal
    (∑ y, Min.min.{0} (p y).toReal (q y).toReal)

declarations.documentation:
Removing each common atom leaves exactly the complement of the overlap.
All subtraction in this identity is truncated `ENNReal` subtraction.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.sum_sub_min_eq_one_sub_overlapMass
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (∑ y, HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (p y) (Min.min.{0} (p y) (q y)))
    (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q))

declarations.documentation: The paper's half-L1 distance is one minus the shared real mass.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_eq_one_sub_overlap_toReal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q)
    (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q).toReal)

declarations.documentation: Exact residual mass and the real total variation describe the same quantity.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_eq_sub_overlap_toReal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q)
    (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q)).toReal

declarations.documentation:
TV is the sum of the positive parts of the atomwise difference.
Each positive part is first formed by truncated `ENNReal` subtraction.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_eq_sum_tsub_toReal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q) (∑ y, (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (p y) (q y)).toReal)

declarations.documentation: Finite total variation is symmetric.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_comm
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q)
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} q p)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem finiteTV_comm (p q : PMF beta) : finiteTV p q = finiteTV q p := by

declarations.documentation: Finite total variation is nonnegative.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_nonneg
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  LE.le.{0} 0 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem finiteTV_nonneg (p q : PMF beta) : 0 ≤ finiteTV p q := by

declarations.documentation: Finite total variation is at most one.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_le_one
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  LE.le.{0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q) 1
declarations.source_line_text: theorem finiteTV_le_one (p q : PMF beta) : finiteTV p q ≤ 1 := by

declarations.documentation: Distance zero means equality of the complete laws, including zero atoms.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_eq_zero_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q) 0 ↔ Eq.{u + 1} p q
declarations.source_line_text: theorem finiteTV_eq_zero_iff (p q : PMF beta) : finiteTV p q = 0 ↔ p = q := by

declarations.documentation: Distance one means that the exact overlap is zero.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV_eq_one_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q) 1 ↔
    Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q) 0

declarations.documentation: Zero overlap is equivalent to a zero pointwise minimum at every label.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass_eq_zero_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q) 0 ↔
    ∀ (y : beta), Eq.{1} (Min.min.{0} (p y) (q y)) 0

declarations.documentation: Zero overlap means disjoint supports, without a full-support premise.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass_eq_zero_iff_disjoint
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q) 0 ↔
    Disjoint.{u} (PMF.support.{u} p) (PMF.support.{u} q)

declarations.documentation: Exact probability that the two coordinates differ, as a finite atom sum.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass
declarations.type: {beta : Type u} → [Fintype.{u} beta] → PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta) → ENNReal
declarations.source_line_text: noncomputable def mismatchMass (g : PMF (beta × beta)) : ℝ≥0∞ := by

declarations.documentation: The finite mismatch sum is the existing PMF outer-measure event probability.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_eq_toOuterMeasure
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g)
    ((PMF.toOuterMeasure.{u} g) (Set.ofPred.{u} fun t => Ne.{u + 1} t.1 t.2))

declarations.documentation: Mismatch and diagonal agreement exhaust the mass of every joint law.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_add_diagonal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  Eq.{1}
    (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g) (∑ y, g (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y)))
    1

declarations.documentation: Exact mismatch is one minus diagonal mass, using truncated subtraction.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_eq_one_sub_diagonal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g)
    (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (∑ y, g (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y)))

declarations.documentation: Exact mismatch never exceeds the total mass one.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_le_one
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  LE.le.{0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g) 1
declarations.source_line_text: theorem mismatchMass_le_one (g : PMF (beta × beta)) : mismatchMass g ≤ 1 := by

declarations.documentation: Mismatch mass is finite, as required for real conversion.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_ne_top
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  Ne.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g) Top.top.{0}
declarations.source_line_text: theorem mismatchMass_ne_top (g : PMF (beta × beta)) : mismatchMass g ≠ ∞ :=

declarations.documentation: Real mismatch is the finite sum of real masses at unequal-coordinate atoms.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_toReal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal
    (∑ t, ite.{1} (Ne.{u + 1} t.1 t.2) (g t).toReal 0)

declarations.documentation: The derived real mismatch is nonnegative.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_toReal_nonneg
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  LE.le.{0} 0 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal

declarations.documentation: The derived real mismatch is at most one.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_toReal_le_one
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  LE.le.{0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal 1

declarations.documentation: The exact agreement/mismatch decomposition also holds for real finite sums.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_toReal_add_diagonal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  Eq.{1}
    (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal
      (∑ y, (g (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y)).toReal))
    1

declarations.documentation: Real mismatch is one minus real diagonal agreement, with ordinary subtraction.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_toReal_eq_one_sub_diagonal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal
    (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (∑ y, (g (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y)).toReal))

declarations.documentation: Diagonal agreement of any coupling is at most the overlap of its marginals.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.sum_diagonal_le_overlapMass
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] {p q : PMF.{u} beta} {g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.{u} p q g →
    LE.le.{0} (∑ y, g (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y)) (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q)

declarations.documentation: Every coupling has at least the complementary overlap mass in mismatch.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.sub_overlapMass_le_mismatchMass
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] {p q : PMF.{u} beta} {g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.{u} p q g →
    LE.le.{0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q))
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g)

declarations.documentation: Total variation bounds the real mismatch of every coupling from below.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.finiteTV_le_mismatchMass_toReal
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] {p q : PMF.{u} beta} {g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.{u} p q g →
    LE.le.{0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q)
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal

declarations.documentation:
The diagonal common mass plus the product of the two residual masses,
divided by their common total. Zero residual mass is handled by ENNReal arithmetic.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling
declarations.type: {beta : Type u} → [Fintype.{u} beta] → PMF.{u} beta → PMF.{u} beta → PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)
declarations.source_line_text: noncomputable def maximalCoupling (p q : PMF beta) : PMF (beta × beta) :=

declarations.documentation: Exact atoms, with a single residual-total denominator.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling_apply
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta) (y z : beta),
  Eq.{1} ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} p q) (Prod.mk.{u, u} y z))
    (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (ite.{1} (Eq.{u + 1} y z) (Min.min.{0} (p y) (q y)) 0)
      (HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0}
        (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (p y) (Min.min.{0} (p y) (q y)))
          (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (q z) (Min.min.{0} (p z) (q z))))
        (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q))))
declarations.source_line_text: theorem maximalCoupling_apply (p q : PMF beta) (y z : beta) :

declarations.documentation: The construction has the two prescribed marginals.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isCoupling_maximalCoupling
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.{u} p q
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} p q)

declarations.documentation: Diagonal agreement is exactly the pointwise common mass.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling_apply_diag
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta) (y : beta),
  Eq.{1} ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} p q) (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y))
    (Min.min.{0} (p y) (q y))
declarations.source_line_text: theorem maximalCoupling_apply_diag (p q : PMF beta) (y : beta) :

declarations.documentation: Total diagonal agreement exhausts the overlap.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.sum_maximalCoupling_diag
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (∑ y, (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} p q) (Prod.mk.{u, u} y y))
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q)

declarations.documentation: Exact mismatch attains the complementary overlap mass.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_maximalCoupling

declarations.documentation: Real mismatch of the constructed coupling attains total variation.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass_maximalCoupling_toReal

declarations.documentation: The coupling minimum is attained, with the universal lower bound included.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.exists_coupling_minimizing_mismatch
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  ∃ g,
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.{u} p q g ∧
      Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal
          (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{u} p q) ∧
        ∀ (g' : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),
          PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCoupling.{u} p q g' →
            LE.le.{0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g).toReal
              (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mismatchMass.{u} g').toReal

declarations.documentation:
Off-diagonal support runs from a strict first-law excess to a strict
second-law excess; equality and zero-mass labels create no residual fibers.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling_apply_pos_iff_of_ne
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta) {y z : beta},
  Ne.{u + 1} y z →
    (LT.lt.{0} 0 ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} p q) (Prod.mk.{u, u} y z)) ↔
      LT.lt.{0} (q y) (p y) ∧ LT.lt.{0} (p z) (q z))
declarations.source_line_text: theorem maximalCoupling_apply_pos_iff_of_ne (p q : PMF beta) {y z : beta}

declarations.documentation: Identical laws give the diagonal pushforward, including at zero-mass labels.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling_self
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{u + 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} p p)
    (PMF.map.{u, u} (fun y => Prod.mk.{u, u} y y) p)

declarations.documentation: With no common mass the construction is the existing independent product.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling_eq_indepProd_of_overlapMass_eq_zero
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (p q : PMF.{u} beta),
  Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} p q) 0 →
    Eq.{u + 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} p q)
      (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.indepProd.{u, u} p q)

declarations.documentation:
Simultaneously mapping both coordinates maps both prescribed marginals.
This elementary coupling property needs neither finiteness nor injectivity.

declarations.documentation:
Independently sample the input and product coupling, then evaluate its vector.
This is equality of full triples, before any marginal or information operation.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint_map_finTwoArrowEquiv_symm
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} (p : PMF.{0} (Fin 2)) (g : PMF.{u} (Prod.{u, u} beta beta)),

      (PMF.map.{u, u} (⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, u + 1} (finTwoArrowEquiv.{u} beta))) g))
    (PMF.map.{u, u}
      (fun xz =>
        Prod.mk.{0, u} xz.1
          (Prod.mk.{u, u} ((Equiv.symm.{u + 1, u + 1} (finTwoArrowEquiv.{u} beta)) xz.2 xz.1)

      (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.indepProd.{0, u} p g))

declarations.documentation:
The common mass in extended (115) is exactly C04 overlap. Both-zero
columns contribute zero, so the shared set need not cover ambient outputs.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.overlapMass_eq_sum_shared
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] {kappa : Fin 2 → PMF.{u} beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{0, u} kappa →
    Eq.{1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} (kappa 0) (kappa 1))
      (∑ y, ite.{1} (Ne.{1} ((kappa 0) y) 0 ∧ Ne.{1} ((kappa 1) y) 0) ((kappa 0) y) 0)

declarations.documentation:
Extended (121), without separately normalizing zero-mass components:
shared diagonal mass plus the exclusive product divided once by the residual
total. C04's construction already handles the overlap-zero/one endpoints.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.maximalCoupling_apply_shared_exclusive
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] {kappa : Fin 2 → PMF.{u} beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{0, u} kappa →
    ∀ (y z : beta),
      Eq.{1} ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} (kappa 0) (kappa 1)) (Prod.mk.{u, u} y z))
        (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0}
          (ite.{1} (Eq.{u + 1} y z)
            (ite.{1} (Ne.{1} ((kappa 0) y) 0 ∧ Ne.{1} ((kappa 1) y) 0) ((kappa 0) y) 0) 0)
          (HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0}
            (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (ite.{1} (Eq.{1} ((kappa 1) y) 0) ((kappa 0) y) 0)
              (ite.{1} (Eq.{1} ((kappa 0) z) 0) ((kappa 1) z) 0))
            (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} 1 (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.overlapMass.{u} (kappa 0) (kappa 1)))))

declarations.documentation:
A singular binary channel's explicit maximal-coupling vector law has one
posterior factoring every row. At globally unused outputs, the selected total
posterior is the vector law itself; no default output is required.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.exists_binary_maximal_commonPosterior
declarations.type:
∀ {beta : Type u} [inst : Fintype.{u} beta] (kappa : Fin 2 → PMF.{u} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{0, u} kappa →
    ∃ V,
      (∀ (i : Fin 2),
          Eq.{u + 1}
            (PMF.map.{u, u} (fun w => Prod.mk.{u, u} (w i) w)
              (PMF.map.{u, u} (⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, u + 1} (finTwoArrowEquiv.{u} beta)))
                (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} (kappa 0) (kappa 1))))
            (PMF.channelJoint.{u, u} (kappa i) V)) ∧
        ∀ (y : beta),
          Eq.{1} ((kappa 0) y) 0 →
            Eq.{1} ((kappa 1) y) 0 →
              Eq.{u + 1} (V y)
                (PMF.map.{u, u} (⇑(Equiv.symm.{u + 1, u + 1} (finTwoArrowEquiv.{u} beta)))
                  (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{u} (kappa 0) (kappa 1)))

declarations.documentation:

declarations.documentation:

declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.mutualInfoOf_le_binary_bound
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {beta : Type v} {gamma : Type w} [inst : Fintype.{v} beta] [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} gamma]
  {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → Fin 2} {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, 0, v, w} mu X Y Z →
    ∀ (p : PMF.{0} (Fin 2)) (kappa : Fin 2 → PMF.{v} beta),
      Eq.{v + 1} (PMF.map.{u, v} (fun s => Prod.mk.{0, v} (X s) (Y s)) mu) (PMF.channelJoint.{0, v} p kappa) →
        LE.le.{0} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, v, w} mu Y Z)
          (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0}
            (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy.{v}
              (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal.{0, v} (PMF.channelJoint.{0, v} p kappa)))
            (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.finiteTV.{v} (kappa 0) (kappa 1))
              (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy.{0} p)))

    Eq.{u + 1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal.{0, u, u} t) (PMF.channelJoint.{0, u} p kappa) ∧
      Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, u, u} t (fun a => a.2.1) fun a => a.2.2)
        (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0}
          (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy.{u}
            (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal.{0, u} (PMF.channelJoint.{0, u} p kappa)))

    PMF.map.{v, max u v} (fun w x => w (e x))

        (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.maximalCoupling.{v} (kappa ((Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} e) 0))
          (kappa ((Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} e) 1))));
  have t := PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{u, v} p q;
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentation.{u, v} t ∧
    Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal.{u, v, max u v} t)

              (kappa ((Equiv.symm.{u + 1, 1} e) 1)))
            (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy.{u} p)))

declarations.documentation:
A functional representation supplies a decoder whose vector is canonical.
The witness remains a deterministic function of the original auxiliary.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.exists_canonical_decoder
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} mu X Y Z →
    ∃ decoder,
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w} mu X Y fun s =>
        PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.decoderVector.{v, w, x} decoder (Z s)

declarations.documentation: A common-source canonical triple agrees with the canonical joint of its laws.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.jointLaw_eq_canonicalJoint
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {W : omega → alpha → beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w} mu X Y W →
    Eq.{max (v + 1) (w + 1)}
      (PMF.map.{u, max v w} (fun s => Prod.mk.{v, max v w} (X s) (Prod.mk.{w, max v w} (Y s) (W s))) mu)
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{v, w} (PMF.map.{u, v} X mu)
        (PMF.map.{u, max v w} W mu))

declarations.documentation: The canonical extension preserves the already specified pair law.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.fstSndMarginal_canonicalJoint

declarations.documentation: A supplied channel agrees with the vector's coordinate laws on input support.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.coordinateLaw_eq_of_mem_support
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {W : omega → alpha → beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w} mu X Y W →
    ∀ (kappa : alpha → PMF.{w} beta),
      Eq.{max (v + 1) (w + 1)} (PMF.map.{u, max w v} (fun s => Prod.mk.{v, w} (X s) (Y s)) mu)
          (PMF.channelJoint.{v, w} (PMF.map.{u, v} X mu) kappa) →
        ∀ (a : alpha),
          Membership.mem.{v, v} (PMF.support.{v} (PMF.map.{u, v} X mu)) a →
            Eq.{w + 1} (PMF.map.{max v w, w} (fun f => f a) (PMF.map.{u, max v w} W mu)) (kappa a)

declarations.documentation: Full input support upgrades the coordinate laws to an all-row coupling.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.isCanonicalCoupling_of_fullSupport
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {W : omega → alpha → beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w} mu X Y W →
    ∀ (kappa : alpha → PMF.{w} beta),
      Eq.{max (v + 1) (w + 1)} (PMF.map.{u, max w v} (fun s => Prod.mk.{v, w} (X s) (Y s)) mu)
          (PMF.channelJoint.{v, w} (PMF.map.{u, v} X mu) kappa) →
        (∀ (a : alpha), Membership.mem.{v, v} (PMF.support.{v} (PMF.map.{u, v} X mu)) a) →
          PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalCoupling.{v, w} kappa (PMF.map.{u, max v w} W mu)

declarations.documentation:
Property 4 and Lemma 1: canonicalization through any support-correct decoder
preserves information about the output at the finite-value boundary.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mutualInfoOf_decoderVector_eq
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [Finite.{v + 1} alpha]
  [inst : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_1 : Fintype.{x} gamma] [inst_2 : Fintype.{max v w} (alpha → beta)]
  (mu : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha) (Y : omega → beta) (Z : omega → gamma)
  (decoder : Prod.{v, x} alpha gamma → beta),
  LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependentOf.{u, v, x} mu X Z →
    (∀ (s : omega),
        Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} mu) s →
          Eq.{w + 1} (Y s) (decoder (Prod.mk.{v, x} (X s) (Z s)))) →
      Eq.{1}
        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, max w v} mu Y fun s =>
          PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.decoderVector.{v, w, x} decoder (Z s))
        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, x} mu Y Z)

declarations.documentation:
A finite functional representation admits an equally informative canonical
replacement of the same pair on the same, unrestricted source.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.exists_canonical_preserving_mutualInfo
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [Finite.{v + 1} alpha]
  [inst : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_1 : Fintype.{x} gamma] [inst_2 : Fintype.{max v w} (alpha → beta)]
  {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha} {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} mu X Y Z →
    ∃ W,
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w} mu X Y W ∧
        Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, max v w} mu Y W)
          (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, x} mu Y Z)

declarations.documentation:
Any support-correct decoder of a finite perfect auxiliary produces a perfect
canonical auxiliary for the same pair.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.decoderVector
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] [inst_3 : Fintype.{max v w} (alpha → beta)]
  {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha} {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} mu X Y Z →
    ∀ (decoder : Prod.{v, x} alpha gamma → beta),
      (∀ (s : omega),
          Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} mu) s →
            Eq.{w + 1} (Y s) (decoder (Prod.mk.{v, x} (X s) (Z s)))) →
        PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, max w v} mu X Y
          fun s => PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.decoderVector.{v, w, x} decoder (Z s)

declarations.documentation:
A specified finite perfect auxiliary has a canonical perfect replacement
without changing its source, input or output.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.exists_canonical
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] [inst_3 : Fintype.{max v w} (alpha → beta)]
  {mu : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha} {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} mu X Y Z →
    ∃ W,
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w} mu X Y W ∧
        PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, max v w} mu X Y W

declarations.documentation:
At C01's finite-information boundary, perfect pair representability is
equivalent to a perfect canonical joint with exactly the specified pair marginal.
This keeps C01's `Fin n` witness predicate unchanged.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentablePair_iff_exists_canonicalJoint

declarations.documentation:
A channel is perfectly representable when one vector law and one posterior
factor every coordinate joint law. The input alphabet is nonempty; no prior,
finite alphabet or full output support is part of this structural definition.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel
declarations.type: {alpha : Type u} → {beta : Type v} → [Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] → (alpha → PMF.{v} beta) → Prop
declarations.source_line_text: def IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Nonempty alpha]

declarations.documentation: Coordinate factorization implies the coupling condition by first projection.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isCanonicalCoupling_of_coordinateFactorization
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)
  (V : beta → PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)),
  (∀ (a : alpha),
      Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
        (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V)) →
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalCoupling.{u, v} kappa q

declarations.documentation: For a fixed posterior, a prior sees exactly the supported coordinate factorizations.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint_eq_channelExtension_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (p : PMF.{u} alpha) (q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta))
  (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (V : beta → PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)),
  Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{u, v} p q)
      (PMF.channelExtension.{u, v, max u v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa) V) ↔
    ∀ (a : alpha),
      Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) a →
        Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
          (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem canonicalJoint_eq_channelExtension_iff {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation: Full input support upgrades fixed-posterior factorization to every input row.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint_eq_channelExtension_iff_of_fullSupport
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (p : PMF.{u} alpha) (q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta))
  (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (V : beta → PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)),
  (∀ (a : alpha), Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) a) →
    (Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{u, v} p q)
        (PMF.channelExtension.{u, v, max u v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa) V) ↔
      ∀ (a : alpha),
        Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
          (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V))

declarations.documentation: One common posterior yields a canonical Markov triple under every prior.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isMarkovChain_canonicalJoint_of_coordinateFactorization
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] (p : PMF.{u} alpha)
  (q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (V : beta → PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)),
  (∀ (a : alpha),
      Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
        (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V)) →
    LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsMarkovChain.{u, v, max v u}
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{u, v} p q)

declarations.documentation:
For a fixed coupling and a full-support prior, canonical Markov factorization
is equivalent to one posterior for all channel rows. Finite function alphabet
is needed only for extracting the posterior from the pinned Markov theorem.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalCoupling.exists_commonPosterior_iff_isMarkovChain
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [Finite.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (alpha → beta)]
  {kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta} {q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalCoupling.{u, v} kappa q →
    ∀ (p : PMF.{u} alpha),
      (∀ (a : alpha), Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) a) →
        ((∃ V,
            ∀ (a : alpha),
              Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
                (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V)) ↔
          LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsMarkovChain.{u, v, max v u}
            (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{u, v} p q))

declarations.documentation:
Changing a posterior only at outputs unused by every row preserves the
coordinate factorizations. No uniqueness at null output fibers is asserted.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.coordinateFactorization_congr_posterior
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)
  (V V' : beta → PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)),
  (∀ (b : beta),
      (∃ a, Membership.mem.{v, v} (PMF.support.{v} (kappa a)) b) → Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (V b) (V' b)) →
    ((∀ (a : alpha),
        Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
          (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V)) ↔
      ∀ (a : alpha),
        Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
          (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V'))
declarations.source_line_text: theorem coordinateFactorization_congr_posterior {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation:
A canonical joint already has the structural representation property, so
its finite perfectness is equivalent to the Markov condition.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectFunctionalRepresentation_canonicalJoint_iff_isMarkovChain

declarations.documentation:
One common posterior yields a perfect canonical triple for any input prior
at the finite-information boundary.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectFunctionalRepresentation_canonicalJoint_of_coordinateFactorization
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{v} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{max u v} (alpha → beta)] (p : PMF.{u} alpha)
  (q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (V : beta → PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)),
  (∀ (a : alpha),
      Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun f => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (f a) f) q)
        (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa a) V)) →
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentation.{u, v, max v u}
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{u, v} p q)

declarations.documentation:
One coupling law gives perfect canonical joints for every prior. The
coupling's pair-marginal theorem identifies the same channel under each prior.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.exists_canonicalCoupling
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_2 : Fintype.{v} beta] [inst_3 : Fintype.{max u v} (alpha → beta)] {kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa →
    ∃ q,
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsCanonicalCoupling.{u, v} kappa q ∧
        ∀ (p : PMF.{u} alpha),
          PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentation.{u, v, max v u}
            (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.canonicalJoint.{u, v} p q)

declarations.documentation:
An intrinsically perfect channel gives a perfectly representable pair
under every prior, including priors with zero-probability inputs.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.isPerfectlyRepresentablePair
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_2 : Fintype.{v} beta] {kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa →
    ∀ (p : PMF.{u} alpha),
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa)

declarations.documentation:
Pair perfectness under a specified full-support prior is equivalent to
the intrinsic channel property. The converse uses finite canonical sufficiency
before extracting the common posterior.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentablePair_channelJoint_iff_of_fullSupport
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_2 : Fintype.{v} beta] (p : PMF.{u} alpha) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  (∀ (a : alpha), Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) a) →
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa) ↔
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa)

declarations.documentation:
Channel perfectness is equivalent to pair perfectness under every prior.
Nonempty finite input supplies a uniform full-support prior for the converse.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentableChannel_iff_forall_prior
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_2 : Fintype.{v} beta] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa ↔
    ∀ (p : PMF.{u} alpha),
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa)

declarations.documentation: It suffices that one full-support prior give a perfectly representable pair.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentableChannel_iff_exists_fullSupport_prior
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_2 : Fintype.{v} beta] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa ↔
    ∃ p,
      (∀ (a : alpha), Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) a) ∧
        PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa)

declarations.documentation:
Changing between full-support input priors preserves pair perfectness
for the same channel. No assumption on output support is required.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentablePair_channelJoint_congr_prior
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{v} beta] (p p' : PMF.{u} alpha) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  (∀ (a : alpha), Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) a) →
    (∀ (a : alpha), Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p') a) →
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v}
          (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa) ↔
        PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v}
          (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p' kappa))

declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.isPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} [inst : Nonempty.{v + 1} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{v} alpha] [inst_2 : Fintype.{w} beta] {kappa : alpha → PMF.{w} beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{v, w} kappa →
    ∀ (mu : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha) (Y : omega → beta) (p : PMF.{v} alpha),
      Eq.{max (v + 1) (w + 1)} (PMF.map.{u, max w v} (fun s => Prod.mk.{v, w} (X s) (Y s)) mu)
          (PMF.channelJoint.{v, w} p kappa) →
        PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf.{u, v, w} mu X Y

declarations.documentation: The normalized input law on its own support, with no finite-alphabet requirement.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.inputSupportPrior
declarations.type: {alpha : Type u} → (p : PMF.{u} alpha) → PMF.{u} ↑(PMF.support.{u} p)
declarations.source_line_text: noncomputable def inputSupportPrior {alpha : Type u} (p : PMF alpha) : PMF p.support :=

declarations.documentation: Every value of the support subtype has positive mass under the restricted prior.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mem_support_inputSupportPrior
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} (p : PMF.{u} alpha) (s : ↑(PMF.support.{u} p)),
  Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.inputSupportPrior.{u} p)) s
declarations.source_line_text: theorem mem_support_inputSupportPrior {alpha : Type u} (p : PMF alpha) (s : p.support) :

declarations.documentation: Inclusion recovers exactly the original input law.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.map_val_inputSupportPrior
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} (p : PMF.{u} alpha),
  Eq.{u + 1} (PMF.map.{u, u} Subtype.val.{u + 1} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.inputSupportPrior.{u} p)) p
declarations.source_line_text: @[simp] theorem map_val_inputSupportPrior {alpha : Type u} (p : PMF alpha) :

declarations.documentation:
Restricting the input prior and channel, then including the input, recovers
the original pair law, including when the prior has zero-probability inputs.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.channelJoint_inputSupportPrior_map_val
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (p : PMF.{u} alpha) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)}
    (PMF.map.{max u v, max v u} (fun sb => Prod.mk.{u, v} (↑sb.1) sb.2)
      (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.inputSupportPrior.{u} p) fun s => kappa ↑s))
    (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem channelJoint_inputSupportPrior_map_val {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation:
Perfect-pair representability is unchanged by restricting the input law to
its support. The proof transports finite witnesses in both directions across
`Subtype.val`; it does not identify the two input types.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentablePair_channelJoint_iff_inputSupportPrior
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{v} beta] (p : PMF.{u} alpha)
  [inst_2 : Fintype.{u} ↑(PMF.support.{u} p)] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa) ↔
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v}
      (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.inputSupportPrior.{u} p) fun s => kappa ↑s)

declarations.documentation:
For an arbitrary finite input prior, perfect-pair representability is exactly
the intrinsic property of the channel restricted to that prior's input support.
The PMF supplies nonemptiness of its support; no ambient full-support premise or
caller-chosen default output is needed.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentablePair_channelJoint_iff_restrict_support
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{v} beta] (p : PMF.{u} alpha)

    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} fun s => kappa ↑s

declarations.documentation:
A triple law is a functional representation when its first and third
coordinates are independent and its second coordinate is a function of the
first and third coordinates on the law's support. The product is Lean's
right-associated `alpha × (beta × gamma)`, with projections `t.1`, `t.2.1`,
and `t.2.2` in that order.

{alpha : Type u} →
  {beta : Type v} →
    {gamma : Type w} → PMF.{max (max w v) u} (Prod.{u, max w v} alpha (Prod.{v, w} beta gamma)) → Prop

declarations.documentation:
Random variables form a functional representation when their full triple
pushforward law is a functional representation. Decoder correctness is required
only on the support of that law.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf
declarations.type:
{omega : Type u} →
  {alpha : Type v} →
    {beta : Type w} →
      {gamma : Type x} → PMF.{u} omega → (omega → alpha) → (omega → beta) → (omega → gamma) → Prop

declarations.documentation:
The common-base structural predicate expands to independence of `X` and `Z`
and existence of a decoder correct on the source PMF's support.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isFunctionalRepresentationOf_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} (p : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha)
  (Y : omega → beta) (Z : omega → gamma),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} p X Y Z ↔
    LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependentOf.{u, v, x} p X Z ∧
      ∃ decoder,
        ∀ (omega_1 : omega),
          Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) omega_1 →
            Eq.{w + 1} (Y omega_1) (decoder (Prod.mk.{v, x} (X omega_1) (Z omega_1)))

declarations.documentation:
Functional representation transports between source spaces with the same full
triple law, preserving the support-correct decoder condition.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isFunctionalRepresentationOf_congr_jointLaw

declarations.documentation: Deterministic postprocessing of `Z` preserves its independence from `X`.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isIndependentOf_comp_right

  (Z : omega → gamma) (f : gamma → delta),
  LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependentOf.{u, v, w} p X Z →
    LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependentOf.{u, v, x} p X fun omega => f (Z omega)

declarations.documentation:
Equation (1): finite-valued variables form a functional representation exactly
when `I(X;Z)` and `H(Y|(X,Z))` vanish. The source type is unrestricted, and the
decoder supplied by zero conditional entropy is existential and correct only
on source support, not an arbitrary preselected decoder.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isFunctionalRepresentationOf_iff_zero_conditions
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] (p : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha)
  (Y : omega → beta) (Z : omega → gamma),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} p X Y Z ↔
    Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, v, x} p X Z) 0 ∧
      Eq.{1}
        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, max x v} p Y fun omega =>
          Prod.mk.{v, x} (X omega) (Z omega))
        0

declarations.documentation:
Equation (2): the unconditional decomposition
`I(Y;Z) = H(Y|X) - I(X;Z|Y) - H(Y|(X,Z)) + I(X;Z)` for finite-valued
variables. The source type is unrestricted; no functional-representation
hypothesis is required.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.mutualInfoOf_eq_pfr_decomposition
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] (p : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha)
  (Y : omega → beta) (Z : omega → gamma),
  Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, x} p Y Z)
    (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0}
      (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0}
        (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, v} p Y X)
          (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf.{u, v, x, w} p X Z Y))
        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, max x v} p Y fun omega =>
          Prod.mk.{v, x} (X omega) (Z omega)))
      (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, v, x} p X Z))

declarations.documentation:
Equation (3): a functional representation satisfies
`I(Y;Z) = H(Y|X) - I(X;Z|Y)`. Value alphabets are finite, the source is
unrestricted, and the structural hypothesis requires decoding only on support.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.mutualInfoOf_eq_condEntropyOf_sub_condMutualInfoOf
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] {p : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} p X Y Z →
    Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, x} p Y Z)
      (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, v} p Y X)
        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf.{u, v, x, w} p X Z Y))

declarations.documentation: Equation (3)'s upper bound for finite-valued, support-aware functional representations.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.mutualInfoOf_le_condEntropyOf
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] {p : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} p X Y Z →
    LE.le.{0} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, x} p Y Z)
      (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, v} p Y X)

declarations.documentation:
Under a finite-valued, support-aware functional representation, equality in
Equation (3)'s upper bound is equivalent to `I(X;Z|Y) = 0`.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.mutualInfoOf_eq_condEntropyOf_iff_condMutualInfoOf_eq_zero
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] {p : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} p X Y Z →
    (Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, x} p Y Z)
        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, v} p Y X) ↔
      Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf.{u, v, x, w} p X Z Y) 0)

declarations.documentation:
Under a finite-valued, support-aware functional representation, equality in
Equation (3)'s upper bound is equivalent to the Markov chain `X → Y → Z`.
No conditional distribution is chosen on null `Y` fibers.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsFunctionalRepresentationOf.mutualInfoOf_eq_condEntropyOf_iff_isMarkovChainOf
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]

        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, v} p Y X) ↔

declarations.documentation:
A finite triple law is perfect when it is a support-aware functional
representation and satisfies `I(Y;Z) = H(Y|X)`. Coordinates of the
right-associated triple are `X = t.1`, `Y = t.2.1`, and `Z = t.2.2`.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentation

{alpha : Type u} →

    {gamma : Type w} →
      [Fintype.{u} alpha] →
        [Fintype.{v} beta] →
          [Fintype.{w} gamma] →
            PMF.{max (max w v) u} (Prod.{u, max w v} alpha (Prod.{v, w} beta gamma)) → Prop

declarations.documentation:
The specified finite-valued auxiliary is perfect when the full triple law is
perfect. Decoding is required only on support; the source type is unrestricted.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf
declarations.type:
{omega : Type u} →
  {alpha : Type v} →
    {beta : Type w} →
      {gamma : Type x} →
        [Fintype.{v} alpha] →

            [Fintype.{x} gamma] → PMF.{u} omega → (omega → alpha) → (omega → beta) → (omega → gamma) → Prop

declarations.documentation: Fixed perfectness is support-aware functional representation plus `I(Y;Z) = H(Y|X)`.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] (p : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha)
  (Y : omega → beta) (Z : omega → gamma),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} p X Y Z ↔

      Eq.{1} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf.{u, w, x} p Y Z)
        (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf.{u, w, v} p Y X)

declarations.documentation: Fixed perfectness retains structural representation as well as `I(X;Z|Y) = 0`.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf_iff_condMutualInfoOf_eq_zero
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]

declarations.documentation: Fixed perfectness retains support-aware representation as well as `X → Y → Z`.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf_iff_isMarkovChainOf
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] (p : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha)
