declarations.documentation: Fixed perfectness transports across source spaces with equal full triple laws.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf_congr_jointLaw

declarations.documentation:
A pair law is perfectly representable at the finite-information boundary when
it has a perfect triple-law extension with auxiliary `Fin n`. This new law
allows probability-space enlargement. Its PMF already excludes `n = 0`.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair
declarations.type:
{alpha : Type u} →
  {beta : Type v} → [Fintype.{u} alpha] → [Fintype.{v} beta] → PMF.{max v u} (Prod.{u, v} alpha beta) → Prop

declarations.documentation:
Perfect representability depends on the pair pushforward law, not on an
auxiliary map existing on the original, unrestricted source space.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf
declarations.type:
{omega : Type u} →
  {alpha : Type v} →
    {beta : Type w} →
      [Fintype.{v} alpha] → [Fintype.{w} beta] → PMF.{u} omega → (omega → alpha) → (omega → beta) → Prop

declarations.documentation: Extract or supply a perfect finite triple-law extension of the given pair law.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf_iff_exists_fin_extension
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta]
  (p : PMF.{u} omega) (X : omega → alpha) (Y : omega → beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf.{u, v, w} p X Y ↔
    ∃ n q,
      Eq.{max (v + 1) (w + 1)} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal.{v, w, 0} q)
          (PMF.map.{u, max w v} (fun omega => Prod.mk.{v, w} (X omega) (Y omega)) p) ∧
        PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentation.{v, w, 0} q

declarations.documentation: Pair perfect representability transports using only equality of pair laws.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf_congr_pairLaw
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {omega' : Type v} {alpha : Type w} {beta : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{w} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{x} beta] {p : PMF.{u} omega} {p' : PMF.{v} omega'} {X : omega → alpha} {Y : omega → beta}
  {X' : omega' → alpha} {Y' : omega' → beta},
  Eq.{max (w + 1) (x + 1)} (PMF.map.{u, max x w} (fun omega => Prod.mk.{w, x} (X omega) (Y omega)) p)
      (PMF.map.{v, max x w} (fun omega => Prod.mk.{w, x} (X' omega) (Y' omega)) p') →
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf.{u, w, x} p X Y ↔
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf.{v, w, x} p' X' Y')

declarations.documentation:
Any finite perfect auxiliary, in any universe, gives a perfect pair-law
extension by relabeling it as `Fin (Fintype.card gamma)` and transporting its
support-correct decoder through the inverse equivalence.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentation.isPerfectlyRepresentablePair
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} {gamma : Type w} [inst : Fintype.{u} alpha] [inst_1 : Fintype.{v} beta]
  [inst_2 : Fintype.{w} gamma] {q : PMF.{max (max w v) u} (Prod.{u, max w v} alpha (Prod.{v, w} beta gamma))},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentation.{u, v, w} q →
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePair.{u, v}
      (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal.{u, v, w} q)

declarations.documentation: A specified finite perfect auxiliary witnesses perfect representability of its pair.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.isPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf
declarations.type:
∀ {omega : Type u} {alpha : Type v} {beta : Type w} {gamma : Type x} [inst : Fintype.{v} alpha]
  [inst_1 : Fintype.{w} beta] [inst_2 : Fintype.{x} gamma] {p : PMF.{u} omega} {X : omega → alpha}
  {Y : omega → beta} {Z : omega → gamma},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectFunctionalRepresentationOf.{u, v, w, x} p X Y Z →
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentablePairOf.{u, v, w} p X Y

declarations.documentation:
A channel is singular when any two nonzero entries in one output column agree.
No finiteness, nonempty alphabet or input law is needed for this predicate.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel
declarations.type: {alpha : Type u} → {beta : Type v} → (alpha → PMF.{v} beta) → Prop
declarations.source_line_text: def IsSingularChannel {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation: Definition 3's positive-product formulation is exactly intrinsic singularity.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isSingularChannel_iff_mul_pos
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa ↔
    ∀ (x1 x2 : alpha) (y : beta),
      LT.lt.{0} 0 (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} ((kappa x1) y) ((kappa x2) y)) → Eq.{1} ((kappa x1) y) ((kappa x2) y)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem isSingularChannel_iff_mul_pos {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation:
Under a common-posterior factorization, each supported posterior vector has
coordinate `y` at every input whose row can emit `y`. Reused by the direct
nonrepresentability example; no finite-alphabet assumption is needed.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.coordinate_eq_of_posterior_support
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (q : PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)
  (V : beta → PMF.{max u v} (alpha → beta)),
  (∀ (x : alpha),
      Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (PMF.map.{max u v, max u v} (fun w => Prod.mk.{v, max u v} (w x) w) q)
        (PMF.channelJoint.{v, max u v} (kappa x) V)) →
    ∀ {x : alpha} {y : beta} {w : alpha → beta},
      Ne.{1} ((kappa x) y) 0 →
        Membership.mem.{max u v, max u v} (PMF.support.{max u v} (V y)) w → Eq.{v + 1} (w x) y

declarations.documentation:
Perfect representability forces intrinsic singularity. The same posterior
atom compares both positive entries, so no prior or finite-alphabet hypothesis
is needed. Nonempty input is inherited from the channel-perfectness contract.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.isSingular
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] {kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta},
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa →
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa

declarations.documentation:
Adding output symbols through an injection preserves intrinsic singularity.
Columns outside the image have zero mass in every row.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isSingularChannel_map_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} {gamma : Type v'} [Finite.{u + 1} alpha] [Finite.{v + 1} beta]
  [Finite.{v' + 1} gamma] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (j : beta → gamma),
  Function.Injective.{v + 1, v' + 1} j →
    ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v'} fun x => PMF.map.{v, v'} j (kappa x)) ↔
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem isSingularChannel_map_iff {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} {gamma : Type v'}

declarations.documentation:
Injective output extension preserves the complete common-posterior witness.
In either direction both components of each coordinate/vector joint law are
pushed forward. The inverse's values away from the image only choose a valid
completion at unused outputs; no default output is a public assumption.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentableChannel_map_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} {gamma : Type v'} [Finite.{u + 1} alpha] [Finite.{v + 1} beta]
  [Finite.{v' + 1} gamma] [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (j : beta → gamma),
  Function.Injective.{v + 1, v' + 1} j →
    ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v'} fun x =>
        PMF.map.{v, v'} j (kappa x)) ↔
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa)

declarations.documentation:
Finite input/output relabeling uses the inverse input equivalence and the
forward output equivalence. Either equivalence may be the identity.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isSingularChannel_relabel_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {alpha' : Type u'} {beta : Type v} {beta' : Type v'} [Finite.{u + 1} alpha]
  [Finite.{u' + 1} alpha'] [Finite.{v + 1} beta] [Finite.{v' + 1} beta'] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta)
  (eX : Equiv.{u + 1, u' + 1} alpha alpha') (eY : Equiv.{v + 1, v' + 1} beta beta'),
  (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u', v'} fun x' =>
      PMF.map.{v, v'} (⇑eY) (kappa ((Equiv.symm.{u + 1, u' + 1} eX) x'))) ↔
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa

declarations.documentation:
Relabeling transports both the canonical vector law and its common
posterior. Nonempty target input is transferred along the input equivalence.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentableChannel_relabel_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {alpha' : Type u'} {beta : Type v} {beta' : Type v'} [Finite.{u + 1} alpha]
  [Finite.{u' + 1} alpha'] [Finite.{v + 1} beta] [Finite.{v' + 1} beta'] [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha]
  (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (eX : Equiv.{u + 1, u' + 1} alpha alpha')
  (eY : Equiv.{v + 1, v' + 1} beta beta'),
  have this := Nonempty.map.{u + 1, u' + 1} (⇑eX) inst;
  (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u', v'} fun x' =>
      PMF.map.{v, v'} (⇑eY) (kappa ((Equiv.symm.{u + 1, u' + 1} eX) x'))) ↔
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa

declarations.documentation: Outputs with positive mass in at least one row, independent of any input law.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs

declarations.source_line_text: def activeOutputs {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (kappa : alpha → PMF beta) : Set beta :=

declarations.documentation:
Restrict each row to globally active outputs by attaching support proofs.
No renormalization, finiteness or chosen default is required.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.restrictActiveOutputs
declarations.type:
{alpha : Type u} →
  {beta : Type v} →
    (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) →

declarations.source_line_text: theorem map_val_restrictActiveOutputs {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation: Restriction preserves each active output mass without scaling.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.restrictActiveOutputs_apply
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta) (x : alpha)
  (a : ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa)),
  Eq.{1} ((PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.restrictActiveOutputs.{u, v} kappa x) a) ((kappa x) ↑a)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem restrictActiveOutputs_apply {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation: A nonempty input supplies a row and therefore an active output.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs_nonempty
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  Set.Nonempty.{v} (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa)
declarations.source_line_text: theorem activeOutputs_nonempty {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Nonempty alpha]

declarations.documentation: Every output of the restricted channel is active in some row.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs_restrictActiveOutputs
declarations.source_line_text: theorem activeOutputs_restrictActiveOutputs {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v}

declarations.documentation: Deleting globally unused outputs preserves singularity at the finite boundary.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isSingularChannel_restrictActiveOutputs_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Finite.{u + 1} alpha] [Finite.{v + 1} beta]
  (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v}
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.restrictActiveOutputs.{u, v} kappa) ↔
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa

declarations.documentation:
Deleting globally unused outputs preserves the complete common-posterior
perfectness property. The only nonempty assumption is on the input.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentableChannel_restrictActiveOutputs_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Finite.{u + 1} alpha] [Finite.{v + 1} beta]
  [inst : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v}
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.restrictActiveOutputs.{u, v} kappa) ↔
    PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa

declarations.documentation:
Under full input support, the pair's output support is the intrinsic union
of all channel rows. A degenerate prior requires C02's input-support restriction.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.support_sndMarginal_channelJoint_eq_activeOutputs_of_fullSupport
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} (p : PMF.{u} alpha) (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  (∀ (x : alpha), Membership.mem.{u, u} (PMF.support.{u} p) x) →
    Eq.{v + 1} (PMF.support.{v} (LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal.{u, v} (PMF.channelJoint.{u, v} p kappa)))
      (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa)

declarations.documentation:
On a finite output alphabet of cardinality at most two, singularity is
equivalent to perfect representability. Singleton outputs are included.
declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentableChannel_iff_isSingular_of_card_le_two
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Fintype.{u} alpha] [inst : Fintype.{v} beta]
  [inst_1 : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  LE.le.{0} (Fintype.card.{v} beta) 2 →
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa ↔
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa)

declarations.name: PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.isPerfectlyRepresentableChannel_iff_isSingular_of_activeOutputs_card_le_two
declarations.type:
∀ {alpha : Type u} {beta : Type v} [Fintype.{u} alpha] [inst : Fintype.{v} beta]
  [inst_1 : Nonempty.{u + 1} alpha] (kappa : alpha → PMF.{v} beta),
  have this := Fintype.ofFinite.{v} ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa);
  LE.le.{0} (Fintype.card.{v} ↑(PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.activeOutputs.{u, v} kappa)) 2 →
    (PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsPerfectlyRepresentableChannel.{u, v} kappa ↔
      PerfectFunctionalRepresentations.IsSingularChannel.{u, v} kappa)
